title: Raw coordinate weighted-product obstruction for the finite Q3 quartic form
question: Does the raw coordinate multiplier q preserve the quartic Friedrichs form domain, or is K^(1/2) q K^(-1/2) necessarily unbounded?

model.test_family: psi_R is the normalized Gaussian with density variance 1/2 and center R
model.obstruction: E0 has degree four with leading coefficient g/4, E1 has degree six with the same leading coefficient g/4, so E1/E0 is asymptotic to R^2 and the raw coordinate weighted product is unbounded
model.scope: one-site shifted onsite form; adding nonnegative bonds cannot repair the one-site high-coordinate obstruction

adversarial_review.check: The translated Gaussian moments are generated from variance 1/2 and the exact centered-moment recurrence, not pasted asymptotic numbers.
The derivative of q psi is included exactly; dropping it would understate E1 but cannot remove the degree-six potential term.
Both leading coefficients are recomputed from the same quartic coefficient g/4, giving the exact ratio-one coefficient after dividing by R^2.
The obstruction is already present in the one-site onsite form; nonnegative bonds only increase the weighted energy and do not provide a cancellation.
The failure is only for the raw coordinate weighted product; bounded Lipschitz multipliers remain closed and resolvent-smoothed polynomials are not decided here.
No modular, common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion is drawn from this route-local obstruction.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks exact leading-coefficient arithmetic only; it does not formalize Gaussian integration or an operator-domain theorem.

qft_interface.closed: A named route-local obstruction: the raw coordinate is not a bounded weighted form multiplier for the quartic shifted form.
qft_interface.open: Resolvent-smoothed polynomial cylinders, modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Negative bounded-product route only; no heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner.

no_overclaim: This is a route-local obstruction for the raw coordinate multiplier in the one-site quartic form. It does not exclude bounded Lipschitz cylinders, resolvent-smoothed polynomials, or other weighted algebras, and it is not a QFT nonexistence theorem.
